transcript.text: I need to flag a conflicts issue before we submit this response. My conflict review, completed this morning, found that the company's existing investigator previously represented a procurement witness in an unrelated matter involving the same allegations. Because of this conflict, the investigator must be removed and the factual investigation must be re-performed by an independent investigator. I have not yet updated the matter's conflict log because the review was just completed this morning. This directly affects our draft response — we cannot represent to the regulator that we are continuing with the existing investigation, and the status update and privilege preservation strategy will need to be revised accordingly.

transcript.text: I need to disclose critical information I confirmed with the regulator's staff this week. Their cooperation protocol grants voluntary-disclosure credit only if the company makes a voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting, produces factual interview summaries prepared by the independent investigator as part of the conflict-driven reinvestigation, and withholds legal advice and attorney work product. The required factual interview summaries must be produced by the independent investigator and submitted with the voluntary disclosure — the reinvestigation is the mechanism for producing those summaries, not a reason to defer, omit, or withhold them. We cannot claim voluntary-disclosure cooperation credit without producing those independent-investigator summaries. The staff emphasized that this fifth-business-day deadline and the factual-summary requirement remain operative even if investigative remediation is needed. I had not circulated this confirmation because it arrived after the response draft was prepared. This is directly relevant to Maya's conflicts flag — the reinvestigation she's describing is actually the mechanism for producing the required summaries, and we need to factor in this fifth-business-day deadline.
